paper_metadata.title: Microalloying effects of Ho on microstructure evolution and high temperature properties of Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: In order to improve high-temperature mechanical properties and oxidation resistance of TiAl alloys, Ho element was added into Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloy.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental methods
evidence.quote: Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloys with Ho content (0, 0.15%, 0.3%), termed C1, C2 and C3 alloys, were fabricated by vacuum arc-melting furnace under argon protection.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure of C1, C2 and C3 alloys
evidence.quote: many white precipitates form in the dendrite gap or within the (α2 + γ) lamellae of C2 alloy, which are identified as Ho2O3 phases by next EDS and TEM analysis.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure of C1, C2 and C3 alloys
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 3(a), elliptical precipitates with size ranging from 1 μm to 3 μm have dispersion distribution in α2/γ lamellae, and Fig. 3(c) shows that the atomic percent of Ho and O in point 1 is 35.13% and 43.55%, respectively, which indicates that fine elliptical precipitates are identified as Ho2O3 particles.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure of C1, C2 and C3 alloys
evidence.quote: When the addition of Ho is 0.15%, Fig. 2(b) indicates that coarse lamellae transform to fine dendrite structure.

evidence.section: 4.2. The antioxidant mechanism of Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloy with 0.15% Ho addition
evidence.quote: There is segregation of Al elements at grain boundaries due to the discharge of Al atoms into the dendrite gap during solidification. As shown in Fig. 2(a) and (b), C2 alloy has larger area of Al segregation compared with C1 alloy.

evidence.section: 4.1. The strengthening mechanism of high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 3(b), Al2Ho phases with large size and more sharp edges form in C3 alloy, and it can be seen that crack source occurs around Al2Ho phases (Fig. 10(b)), which accounts for the decreased tensile strength of C3 alloy.

evidence.quote: compared with C1 alloy, the C2 alloy has lower oxidation rate, which indicates that C2 alloy has better oxidation resistance at 900 °C.

evidence.section: 4.1. The strengthening mechanism of high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: As the size of Ho2O3 particles is at the nanometer-scale, they have Orowan strengthening effect [28].

evidence.section: 4.1. The strengthening mechanism of high-temperature tensile properties
evidence.quote: The interface between matrix and Ho2O3 is clean and straight (Fig. 9(d)), which indicates that Ho2O3 particles in the micron-level could take the load transferring from the matrix.

evidence.section: 4.2. The antioxidant mechanism of Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloy with 0.15% Ho addition
evidence.quote: the segregation of Ho-rich phase at the lamellar colony boundaries of C2 alloy suppresses the inward diffusion of oxygen and impedes the internal oxidation, which leads to the reduction of oxidation rate.

mechanisms.name: better adhesion between oxide film and matrix
mechanisms.material_state: oxidized at 900 °C for 100 h in air

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: 0.15% Ho improved oxidation resistance of Ti46Al4Nb1Mo alloy, which was due to suppression of inward diffusion of oxygen and better adhesion between oxide film and matrix.
